user_state: Confused. Foggy. Can't see the next step. Too many options or no clear direction. Decision fatigue. Feels lost inside their own life.

arrival.heading: The fog is real.
arrival.subheading: It is not permanent. It is the state before something becomes clear.

arrival.heading: You don't need to see all of it.
arrival.subheading: You need to see the next thing. Just the next thing.

arrival.heading: More thinking has not brought the answer.
arrival.subheading: Clarity comes from stopping, not from pushing harder.

arrival.heading: Simple is the direction.
arrival.subheading: Not simple because it is easy. Simple because everything else has been tried.

arrival.heading: You are not lost.
arrival.subheading: You are between two points of clarity. That is a real place. You have been here before.

arrival.heading: The confusion is information.
arrival.subheading: It is telling you something about what is not yet true. That is useful.

arrival.heading: One clear thing.
arrival.subheading: That is all you need right now. Not a plan. One clear thing.

release.heading: What are you confused about?
release.subheading: Write it out without trying to solve it. Just describe the fog.
release.field_placeholder: Describe the confusion as clearly as you can, without looking for the answer...

release.heading: What are all the options you are holding?
release.subheading: List them. Outside the head, they take up less space.
release.field_placeholder: All the options, decisions, or directions competing in your mind right now...

release.heading: What do you already know?
release.subheading: Not what you're unsure of. What you know for certain.
release.field_placeholder: What is already clear, even amid the fog...

release.heading: What are you overthinking?
release.subheading: Name the thing you have been circling for too long.
release.field_placeholder: The decision or situation you have returned to most often without resolution...

release.heading: What does the fog feel like in your body?
release.subheading: Confusion is not just mental. Where do you feel it?
release.field_placeholder: Where in your body does the confusion or uncertainty live...

release.heading: What would help the most right now?
release.subheading: Not the full answer. Just what would help most, right now.
release.field_placeholder: If one thing could shift, what would it be...

release.heading: What do you wish someone would tell you?
release.subheading: Write it. That is often what you already know.
release.field_placeholder: What answer are you looking for that you might already have...

breath.heading: A clearing breath.
breath.instruction: Breathe in through the nose. Long exhale through the mouth. Imagine exhaling the fog. Three times.

breath.heading: Slow the thinking down.
breath.instruction: Breathe in for four counts. Hold for two. Out for six. Repeat. The mind slows when the body slows.

breath.heading: Let the breath reset.
breath.instruction: Close the eyes. Breathe naturally. Focus only on the sensation of breathing. Nothing else. One minute.

breath.heading: Empty the mind with the exhale.
breath.instruction: Inhale gently. Exhale fully. On the exhale, let the thoughts release with the breath. Four cycles.

breath.heading: Arrive here first.
breath.instruction: Before trying to see clearly, arrive here completely. Three slow breaths. Fully in this room.

moment.heading: What is the one thing that needs to become clear today?
What do you actually know, even if you can't see the whole picture?
What is the simplest version of the next step?
What would you do if you trusted what you already know?
What can you simplify right now, in this moment?
What decision has been waiting the longest for clarity?
What is the smallest clear thing you can see from where you stand?

completion.heading: Something cleared.
completion.subheading: Maybe not everything. Something. That is how clarity arrives.

completion.heading: You stopped and the fog shifted.
completion.subheading: More thinking was not the answer. This was.

completion.heading: One clear thing.
completion.subheading: You found it. Or you're closer. Either is progress.

completion.heading: The fog is thinner now.
completion.subheading: Not gone. Just enough visibility to take the next step.

completion.heading: You simplified.
completion.subheading: That is the whole practice. And it works every time you try it.

completion.heading: You stayed with the discomfort of not-knowing.
completion.subheading: That takes more than people realize. The clarity is a reward for that patience.

completion.heading: Clear enough to move.
completion.subheading: That is all clarity ever needs to be. Not certain. Clear enough.

actions.content: Write down everything you are trying to figure out right now. All of it.
actions.why: The confused mind holds too much simultaneously. Writing it separates the strands.

actions.content: Cross out everything on your list that does not need a decision today.
actions.why: Decision fatigue is driven by volume. Reducing the active list restores clarity.

actions.content: Ask yourself: 'What do I already know about this?' Write the answer.
actions.why: The fog often obscures what you already know. Surfacing the known clears space.

actions.content: Simplify the question. Write it in ten words or fewer.
actions.why: When the question is unclear, the answer stays hidden. Short questions are sharper.

actions.content: Write two options for the decision you are stuck on. Circle the one your gut leans toward.
actions.why: Limiting to two forces a lean. The gut often knows before the mind does.

actions.content: Step away from the problem for 20 minutes. Do something physical.
actions.why: The default mode network — where insight lives — is most active during rest.

actions.content: Write a list of your values. Then look at the decision you're stuck on through that lens.
actions.why: Most confusion dissolves when you remember what actually matters to you.

actions.content: Ask someone you trust: 'What would you do in my position?' Listen without defending.
actions.why: An external perspective often sees what proximity obscures.

actions.content: Write: 'I am confused about ___ because ___.' Fill both blanks.
actions.why: Naming the source of confusion often dissolves part of it.

actions.content: Reduce your active to-do list to three items. Only three.
actions.why: Overwhelm is often a list problem, not a capacity problem.

actions.content: Sleep on the decision you are stuck on. Make a note to return to it tomorrow.
actions.why: Sleep is when the brain consolidates information and often resolves what waking can't.

actions.content: Write the decision you are most avoiding making. Then write what you are afraid of.
actions.why: Fear is often what creates fog. Naming the fear is the beginning of clarity.

actions.content: Turn off all input for 30 minutes. No podcasts, music, or content.
actions.why: Constant input prevents the mind from processing what it already has.

actions.content: Draw a simple diagram of the problem. Boxes and arrows. No words needed.
actions.why: Spatial representation of a problem creates distance and reveals structure.

actions.content: Write your instinctive answer to the question you've been overthinking. First thought only.
actions.why: The first answer is often the right one before fear and analysis complicate it.

actions.content: Write what you would tell a friend who was confused about exactly this.
actions.why: Advice to others is often wiser than advice to ourselves. Use that.

actions.content: Reduce your commitments for this week by one. Email someone now to reschedule or decline.
actions.why: Mental fog is often a symptom of too many concurrent obligations.

actions.content: Write what the decision does NOT need to include. Constraints clarify.
actions.why: Knowing what is off the table reduces the option space to something manageable.

actions.content: Say aloud: 'I don't need to know everything. I just need to know this one thing.'
actions.why: Reducing the requirement from everything to one thing is a clarity intervention.

actions.content: Give yourself a deadline for the stuck decision. Even a made-up one.
actions.why: Decisions left open indefinitely stay open indefinitely. A deadline forces resolution.

actions.content: Write a pro/con list for the decision. Then ignore it and notice your gut reaction.
actions.why: Pro/con lists often clarify by showing you which side you hoped would win.

actions.content: Walk outside without headphones. Let the mind wander without direction.
actions.why: Unstructured outdoor movement is one of the most reliable clarity-producing states.

actions.content: Write what would be true if you made a decision today, either way. Imagine both.
actions.why: Future projection is more useful than extended present analysis.

actions.content: Identify one thing you know for certain. State it aloud. Start from there.
actions.why: Clarity builds from the known outward, not from the unknown inward.

actions.content: Journal freely for 10 minutes. No structure. Just write what is in your head.
actions.why: Free writing externalizes the internal noise and often surfaces unexpected clarity.

actions.content: Identify the one decision that would simplify three other decisions if you made it.
actions.why: Not all decisions are equal. The root decision creates the most leverage.

actions.content: Ask: 'In six months, will this decision matter?' If yes, slow down. If not, decide now.
actions.why: Temporal perspective reveals whether the fog is proportional to the actual stakes.

actions.content: Write three things that are currently clear. Focus only on those today.
actions.why: Acting on what is clear is always available, even when the big picture is foggy.

actions.content: Postpone one non-urgent decision until next week. Write it down and close it.
actions.why: Not every open question needs to be resolved today. Selective postponement reduces load.

actions.content: Write one sentence: 'The most important thing right now is ___.' Fill the blank. Trust it.
actions.why: Single-sentence clarity is often more useful than extended analysis.
